card: This pull request checks whether libmultiprocess example targets exist before setting their compile commands properties in CMake. Upstream changes in bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess#287 remove those example targets, causing CMake configuration errors when Bitcoin Core is built against an external libmultiprocess or tested in libmultiprocess CI. The change only affects custom or CI builds against an external libmultiprocess and does not alter default in-tree subtree builds.
evidence: Commit b29f764890 / PR description: Upstream bitcoin-core/libmultiprocess#287 removes example targets, causing 'CMake Error at cmake/libmultiprocess.cmake:37 ... Can not find target to add properties to: mpcalculator'.
Commit b29f764890 / PR description: The check is needed for custom builds with external libmultiprocess and to keep Bitcoin Core CI jobs working in the libmultiprocess repository.
problem: Upstream libmultiprocess PR #287 removes example targets. Building Bitcoin Core against an updated external libmultiprocess fails at CMake configure time with an error that it cannot find the target mpcalculator to add properties to, which also breaks Bitcoin Core CI jobs running within the libmultiprocess repository.
summary: Check whether the example targets mpcalculator, mpprinter, and mpexample exist before setting their EXPORT_COMPILE_COMMANDS property in cmake/libmultiprocess.cmake. This allows CMake configuration to succeed when building against versions of libmultiprocess that do not define those targets.
